name: Evangelsit Damilola Mike-Bamiloye
history: Evangelist Damilola Mike-Bamiloye is a Nigerian Christian filmmaker and the first child of Mike and Gloria Bamiloye. Mount Zion’s film profile says his interest began in childhood by acting out his father’s films, then copying scripts and developing into writing his own movies. His work spans feature films and serial dramas, including The Train, Legion, 30 Pieces, Shackles, Stranded, Magdalene and the Corpers’ Lodge series. The directory distinguishes titles listed in the filmography from direct video links and verified original posters.

name: Evangelist John Oguntuase
history: Evangelsit John Oguntuase is a Nigerian faith-based filmmaker and the CEO of 2nd Touch Production. The Gospel Filmmaking Network describes him as a director, producer, actor and author, with about two decades of experience and more than 15 national and international awards. His work includes both short films and feature-length gospel stories.
productions: 2nd Touch Production / Peculiar Priesthood Production / JITA Studios

name: Evangelist Felix Bankole
history: Evangelist Felix Bankole is a Nigerian Christian filmmaker, playwright, screenwriter, director, cinematographer, film editor, author, and drama missionary. He is the founder and president of Vision Drama Missions Outreach International and the founding president of the Africa Fellowship of Evangelical Drama Ministers and Filmmakers (AFEDRAM). Through drama and filmmaking, he has participated in evangelistic missions across 16 African countries, using more than 20 languages to communicate Christian messages. His notable works include Bayan Wahala, Chalita, Samari, and The Macedonian Call. He is also the founder of Vision Film Academy in Abuja, where he contributes to training emerging filmmakers and promoting Christian filmmaking across Africa.

name: Mount Zion Film Ministry
role: Founding Christian film Organisation · Mount Zion founders
history: The directory's Mount Zion records trace a long-running Nigerian Christian-film tradition from Agbara Nla (1993) and The Perilous Times (1992) through later productions. Mike and Gloria Bamiloye are credited on several foundational titles; Damilola Mike-Bamiloye and other collaborators appear in the later generation of the archive.

name: Evangelist Shola Mike Agboola
history: Evangelist Shola Mike Agboola is a Nigerian gospel filmmaker, actor, screenwriter, director, author, and drama evangelist known for using film and drama to communicate Christian teachings. He is the president of EVOM World Network (Evangelical Vineyard Outreach Ministry), a Christian ministry that began its drama evangelism activities in 1988 and was officially established on March 1, 1989. Born in Samaru, Zaria, Northern Nigeria, Agboola hails from Kwara State. He studied Chemistry at the University of Ilorin and later specialised in Environmental Chemistry at the postgraduate level. Following his Christian conversion in August 1988, he dedicated himself to full-time drama evangelism, choosing film as a medium for spreading the gospel. Over the years, he has written, directed, and acted in numerous Christian films and stage productions. His notable works include Destiny for Sale, Waiting for Time, My Conclusion, My Dream, and Life for Life. Through his ministry and filmmaking, he has contributed to the development of Nigerian gospel cinema and inspired audiences with stories centred on faith, spiritual growth, and Christian living.
imageAlt: Professional studio portrait of Shola Mike

name: Evangelist Mike Bamiloye
history: Evangelist Mike Bamiloye, born on 13 April 1960 in Ilesa, Osun State, Nigeria, is a renowned Nigerian Christian filmmaker, actor, playwright, screenwriter, producer, director, and drama evangelist. He is the founder of Mount Zion Faith Ministries International, established in 1985 to spread the gospel through Christian drama and filmmaking. He is known for producing films that explore faith, salvation, spiritual warfare, holiness, and moral values. Some of his notable productions include Agbara Nla, The Great Mistake, The Beginning of the End, The Train, and Abejoye. He is married to Gloria Bamiloye, a Christian drama minister and filmmaker, and they have three children. Through his films, ministry, and the Mount Zion Institute of Christian Drama, Mike Bamiloye has significantly contributed to the development of Nigerian gospel cinema and inspired generations of Christian filmmakers. Evangelist Mike Bamiloye is widely recognised for his role in developing Nigerian gospel cinema. Through Mount Zion Faith Ministries, he has helped establish Christian drama as a medium for evangelism, biblical education, and moral storytelling. He is a pioneering figure in Nigerian Christian filmmaking whose decades of work in drama, screenwriting, and film production have influenced generations of gospel filmmakers and audiences.
imageAlt: Professional studio portrait of Mike Bamiloye

name: Evangelsit Gloria Bamiloye
history: Evangelist Gloria Bamiloye is a co-founder of Mount Zion Film Productions and a long-standing contributor to Nigerian Christian drama and film. The directory credits her on foundational Mount Zion titles. This profile records the film credits available here without guessing at unverified biographical details.

name: John 316 Film School Foundation
history: Ugandan Christian film training institution founded by Bamulanzeki Geoffrey (VJ Geoffrey). Its official biography says the school grew from a vision to translate and distribute Christian movies to local communities and was formally established in 2022 to train creative professionals in onscreen storytelling.

name: KAC Studios
history: Ghana-based Christian-inspired studio whose team develops faith-rooted stories with broad audience appeal. Ghana News Agency reports that the studio screened The Cleaner, Mirage and The Right to Do Anything at an Accra industry event, with a stated ambition to combine Christian values with cinematic quality and everyday human themes.

name: Matrid Nyagah
organization: Fearless Films / African Christian Visual Media Network
history: Kenyan filmmaker, pastor and storyteller with more than a decade of experience in faith-driven film and immersive media. ICVM describes her as co-founder and executive director of Fearless Films, a mentor to creatives, and a founding member of the African Christian Visual Media Network. The directory includes her credited work on Where the River Divides; other widely known credits are listed as context, not automatically treated as Christian films.

name: Abel Waweru
history: Kenyan filmmaker and editor who founded the Christian International Film Festival Africa. The Standard reports that he has more than 13 years of film and media experience and conceived CIFFA as a bridge between professional filmmaking and Christian faith. His work connects filmmakers and audiences around faith-based storytelling across the continent.

name: Sam Rushimisha
country: Rwanda / DR Congo (based in the United States)
history: Gospel artist Sam Rushimisha, born in DR Congo and raised in Rwanda, introduced his first Christian film Muri Yesu in 2025. InyaRwanda reports that it was released in Kinyarwanda, Swahili, English and Spanish. His profile represents the growing multilingual reach of Christian screen storytelling across African communities and the diaspora.

name: Chim Onyebilanma
history: The African Christian Visual Media Network describes Chim Onyebilanma as a filmmaker and member of the International Academy of Television Arts & Sciences. Through CAP Studios in Durban, he focuses on faith-based Afrocentric stories; the network notes that his feature Treasure Hunt had a South African theatrical release in 2025.
imageAlt: Portrait available through the linked ACVMN profile

name: Daniel James Ofori-Atta
history: Daniel James Ofori-Atta leads KAC Studios, a Christian-inspired production studio working to make faith-rooted stories accessible to audiences beyond church communities. Ghana News Agency reports that KAC Studios screened The Cleaner, Mirage and The Right to Do Anything at an Accra industry event, and describes its mission as combining Christian values with relatable, culturally grounded storytelling.
imageAlt: Portrait available in the linked Ghana News Agency report

name: Evangelist Ayobami Adegboyega
history: Evangelsit Ayobami Adegboyega leads PRODRAM Productions, a faith-based film and drama ministry. PRODRAM describes its work as Christ-centred storytelling focused on biblical truth, family restoration and discipleship. Its official site lists productions including Nicodemeus, Forty XL and Faded Lines.
